results.content:
The survey’s measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the next year jumped to 4.6% from 4.0% last month. Twelve-month inflation expectations were at 3.4% in February before the U.S.-led war with Iran started. Consumers’ expectations for inflation over the next five years edged up 3.4% from 3.3% in August. They are higher than their 2024 range of 2.8% to 3.2%.

results.content: US consumer sentiment fell to its second-lowest level on record in September as high gas prices further soured Americans’ views of the economy. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index for September dipped to 48.1, notching a 7% decline from August and a nearly 13% drop from a year ago, according to data released Friday. After navigating a once-in-a-century global pandemic, US households have had to contend with higher-than-normal inflation – and the compounding effects of fast-rising prices – for the past five and a half years. results.content: Consumer sentiment fell sharply in September as an inflation-weary public took a dimmer view on the labor market and the impact higher prices would have on their finances, the Conference Board reported Tuesday. The board's Consumer Confidence Index tumbled to 81.9, a decline of 6.7 points and a reading well below the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 89. Other readings showed similar deterioration: The board's Present Situation index fell 7.9 points to 109.3, while the Expectations Index, a six-month outlook window, slipped 5.9 points to 63.6.
